cover.title: Docker Complete Notes
cover.subtitle: Platform to ==build, ship and run== apps in containers
cover.tagline: 'Works on my machine' solved: ship the **environment** with the app. Prereqs: basic Linux shell, some idea of processes and ports.

slides.page_title: What Docker Is and Why It Exists

blocks.text: Docker packages an app plus its ==dependencies== into a __container__ that runs the same on any host with a Docker engine.

cards.title: Container
cards.text: Running **instance** of an image; an isolated process

items: App + libs + runtime + config shipped as ==one unit==
Same image runs on laptop, CI runner, prod server
Solves **dependency drift** between dev, test and prod
Kills {red:'works on my machine'}: the machine ships with the app
Container = isolated process sharing the __host kernel__, not a full OS
`dockerd` daemon: builds images, runs containers, exposes a ==REST API==
`docker` CLI is a client; talks to daemon over __Unix socket__ or TCP
dockerd hands lifecycle to ==containerd== (pull, start, stop)
containerd calls `runc`, the **OCI runtime**, to fork the real process
OCI standardizes image + runtime: same image runs on Podman, Kubernetes
Docker = ==standardized== shipping format for apps
Portable: same image, any engine, any host
Lightweight: shared kernel, ms startup, MB images
Image → container → registry; CLI → dockerd → containerd → runc

slides.subtitle: (Containers, Engine, OCI)

blocks.note: pull on any host, identical result

items: Treating a container like a **VM**: web + db + cron in one
Running `sshd` inside; use `docker exec` instead
Expecting a full OS boot; there is no init, only your process
Editing a running container; changes vanish with it

blocks.title: OCI tip
blocks.text: Docker did not invent containers, it packaged them. Because of ==OCI==, an image you build today runs unchanged on Podman or Kubernetes.
A container is not a mini VM: it is an ordinary Linux ==process== that the kernel isolates with __namespaces__, limits with __cgroups__ and feeds a layered filesystem via **overlay2**.

cards.title: Namespaces
cards.text: Own view: pids, net, mounts, hostname

cards.title: cgroups
cards.text: Caps on CPU, memory, IO, pid count

cards.title: Capabilities
cards.text: Root minus dangerous powers; seccomp filters

items: `pid` ns: app is **PID 1** inside, a normal pid (e.g. 48213) on the host
`ps aux` on the host still lists it; `kill` from the host works
Inside, the container sees ==only its own== processes
Same trick as `unshare --pid --fork bash` on bare Linux
cgroups ==limit and account==: CPU shares, memory cap, block IO, pid count
Memory over cap: kernel **OOM kill**, exit code 137, `docker ps` shows Exited
CPU over cap: throttled, not killed; watch `throttled_time`
Files live under `/sys/fs/cgroup/...`; `docker stats` reads them

steps.note: thin, per container, deleted on rm

items: Read: kernel looks ==top-down==, first hit wins
Modify a lower-layer file: **copy-up** into the rw layer first, then write
Delete: a ==whiteout== marker hides it; lower layer never changes
Ten nginx containers share one image; each pays only for its rw layer
Root inside keeps a ==reduced cap set==: no `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, no `CAP_SYS_MODULE`
`--cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE` keeps only port 80 binding
**seccomp** default profile blocks ~44 syscalls (`mount`, `reboot`, `ptrace`...)
**AppArmor** `docker-default` profile denies writes to `/proc` and `/sys`
Custom filter: `--security-opt seccomp=my.json`
Kernel gives PID 1 no default signal handlers: `SIGTERM` is ==ignored== unless handled
`docker stop` waits 10s then `SIGKILL`: unflushed writes lost
Orphaned children become **zombies** unless PID 1 calls `wait()`
`tini` handles both, then forwards signals to your app
container = ==namespaces== (isolation) + ==cgroups== (limits) + ==overlay== layers (filesystem)
Container PID 1 is a normal host process; host `ps` sees it
Memory cap exceeded = OOM kill; CPU cap exceeded = throttle
Copy-on-write: lower layers never change, edits copy up
Defaults drop caps and filter syscalls; kernel is still shared

slides.page_title: The PID 1 Problem and Isolation Limits

blocks.note: PID 1 must reap zombies and catch SIGTERM

items: Treating container isolation as ==VM security==: kernel is shared, a kernel exploit escapes
Expecting native containers on Mac/Windows: **Docker Desktop** runs a Linux VM; containers are Linux processes inside it
Shipping a shell-form CMD as PID 1: signals never reach the app
Running with no `--memory`: one leak can OOM the whole host

blocks.title: Peek inside
blocks.text: On the host run `ls -l /proc/<pid>/ns` to see a container's namespace ids, and `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` inside it to see the cap. Networking namespaces get their own page (9).
An image is the frozen blueprint a container starts from: a stack of ==read-only layers== plus a small JSON config, named by a tag and identified by a digest.

slides.subtitle: (Namespaces, cgroups, Union FS)

items: ==Immutable== read-only template: ordered layers + JSON config
Config holds **entrypoint**, env vars, exposed ports, default cmd
Each layer = tarball of filesystem diffs, ==content-addressed== by SHA256
Two images from the same base share those layers on disk and in the registry

blocks.note: latest = default tag, not newest build

spec.title: Layer Sharing: one base, two images

blocks.note: pull and push move only missing layers

items: `docker rmi` fails: a **stopped** container still references the image; `docker rm` it first
Deploying `:latest` in prod; the tag moved and the app changed overnight
Letting `<none>` dangling images pile up; run `docker image prune`
Assuming same tag = same bytes; only the ==digest== guarantees that
Image = stack of ==content-addressed layers== + JSON config
**Tags point, digests pin**; pin versions to avoid surprise upgrades
Pull, push and registries move only missing layers; same base is stored once
Multi-arch: a manifest list maps one tag to amd64 and arm64 images

blocks.title: Pin it
blocks.text: Use `nginx:1.27` instead of `latest`; for exact reproducibility copy the digest from `docker image inspect` and run `nginx@sha256:...`.
A ==container== is a runnable instance of an image: it gets its own __writable layer__, its own network namespace and its own process tree, with your app as **PID 1**.

cards.title: Container
cards.text: image + writable layer + own net namespace

items: Image is read-only; container adds one thin ==writable layer== on top
Own net namespace: own IP, own port space (see page 9)
States: {green:created}, {green:running}, {orange:paused}, {red:exited}, removed
`docker ps` lists **running** only; `docker ps -a` lists all states
Stopped containers keep their writable layer until `docker rm`

slides.page_title: Run, Stop, Inspect and Restart Policies

items: `docker run` = ==docker create== + ==docker start== in one step
`-d` detaches (runs in background); `-it` gives an interactive **TTY**
`--rm` deletes the container on exit: ideal for one-off commands
`docker stop` sends **SIGTERM**, waits 10s (`-t 30` to change), then SIGKILL
`docker kill` sends **SIGKILL** at once: no grace period

lines: docker exec -it web sh   # new shell

rows: like always, not after manual stop

items: Exit **0**: app finished cleanly
Exit **137** = 128 + 9: killed by SIGKILL, often ==OOM== (page 3)
Exit **143** = 128 + 15: got SIGTERM and shut down
See it with `docker ps -a` or `docker inspect -f '{{.State.ExitCode}}'`

blocks.title: Sticky tip
blocks.text: Name every container (`--name web`). Then every command reads `docker logs web`, `docker exec web`, `docker stop web` instead of a random ID.
A ==Dockerfile== is a plain-text recipe of instructions; `docker build` executes them **top to bottom**, committing a layer per step, to produce an image.

slides.subtitle: (create, run, stop, inspect, clean up)

items: Running `docker run` again and again: each call makes a **new** container; use `docker start web`
App ignores SIGTERM: every stop waits 10s then hard-kills (fix on page 13)
Using `attach` when you wanted `exec`: Ctrl+C stops PID 1
Logging to a file inside the container: `docker logs` shows nothing
Forgetting `--rm` on throwaway runs: `ps -a` fills with exited junk
`docker container prune` removes **all** stopped containers
`docker system prune` also drops unused networks and dangling images
`run` = `create` + `start`; restart old ones with `start`, not `run`
`stop` is polite (SIGTERM, wait), `kill` is instant (SIGKILL)
Set `--restart unless-stopped` on long-running services

cards.title: Dockerfile
cards.text: Text recipe, run top to bottom

cards.title: Build context
cards.text: Files sent to the daemon; the `.`

items: `FROM` sets the ==base image==; must be **first** (only `ARG` may precede); `FROM scratch` = empty base
`RUN` runs a command at __build time__ and commits a **new layer**
Shell form `RUN apt-get ...` wraps in `/bin/sh -c`; exec form `RUN ["apt-get", ...]` runs direct
`COPY` copies context files in; `ADD` also untars local tars and fetches URLs, so **prefer COPY**
`WORKDIR /app` sets cwd for later steps and the container; created if missing

blocks.title: .dockerignore
items: `node_modules` and build output
`.git` history
`.env` and other ==secrets==
Trims the context sent to `dockerd`
`ENV APP_ENV=prod` persists into the container; `ARG VER=1` is ==build-only==, passed with `--build-arg`
`EXPOSE 8000` only **documents** the port; `-p 8000:8000` at run time publishes it
`CMD` = default command, replaced by `docker run` args; `ENTRYPOINT` = fixed executable, `CMD` becomes its args
`USER app` switches to ==non-root== for later steps and runtime; `RUN adduser -D app` first
`LABEL maintainer=iolar` adds metadata; `HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -f localhost` marks healthy / unhealthy
Shell-form `CMD python app.py` runs under `/bin/sh -c`; app never gets **SIGTERM**, stop waits 10s then kills
`ADD` for plain copies: surprise tar extraction or remote fetch
Believing `EXPOSE` publishes; only `-p` maps host ports
No `.dockerignore`: `node_modules`, `.git`, secrets sent to daemon and baked in
Skipping `USER`: app runs as **root** in the container (page 12)
`FROM` first; one layer per `RUN`, `COPY`, `ADD`
Prefer `COPY`; `ADD` only for local tars
`ENV` persists, `ARG` is build-only; `EXPOSE` documents, `-p` publishes
`ENTRYPOINT` fixed exe + `CMD` default args, both ==exec form==
`.dockerignore` and `USER app` on every real image

blocks.title: Exec form, always
blocks.text: `CMD ["python","app.py"]` makes the app **PID 1**, so the SIGTERM from `docker stop` reaches it. Shell form hides it behind `sh -c`.

caption.text: Ever wondered what actually happens when you type docker run? These handwritten notes take you from namespaces and cgroups to Compose, registries and production hardening in one series. Save this carousel, it's your whole Docker study sheet.
